Now speaking

Morning, George — it's Tuesday the eleventh, and it's the heat again, only worse: Athens is heading for about thirty-five today, clear and dry, with that Meltemi wind.

Two things to actually do before the day runs away from you — grab those free Epic games, because they vanish tomorrow, and drink water like it's part of training.

Oh, and a heads-up: there's a total solar eclipse over Europe tomorrow, though you'll barely catch it from here.

— personal items —

Let's start with Ukraine, where the fighting grinds on but the fresh news is really in Washington.

A bipartisan group in the US House just introduced the Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, aimed squarely at Russia's energy revenues, its banks, and the networks it uses to dodge existing sanctions.

On the ground it stays brutal — a Russian missile barrage on Odesa injured at least fourteen people and knocked out power for around three hundred thousand families.

Over in Yemen, Houthi strikes on the Red Sea port of Mokha killed at least eleven people — a reminder that corner of the map is still very much alight while everyone's looking elsewhere.

And for the science file: a new study says the humble potato may have rewritten human DNA.

Indigenous Andeans in Peru carry the highest known count of a starch-digesting gene on the planet, and it started climbing right when they began farming potatoes thousands of years ago.

Diet, literally shaping evolution.

On the AI front, the story is Google stumbling.

It's reshuffling its AI leadership — Demis Hassabis moving up into a bigger strategy-and-science role while someone else runs the day-to-day — as its top-tier Gemini keeps slipping months behind.

Meanwhile OpenAI is reportedly lining up to go public, with its paperwork expected in the next couple of weeks and a listing targeted for September.

And the top of the pile hasn't budged: Claude Opus 5 is still the sharpest model out there for raw intelligence and coding.

So if you see a splashy Gemini launch date floating around, treat it as rumour until it's actually live.

Back to that eclipse.

It's a proper one — a total solar eclipse sweeping across Iceland, northern Spain, and a sliver of Portugal, the first to touch mainland Europe in decades.

The catch for you: from Athens the sun sets before anything really happens, so you'll see essentially nothing.

Only the far northwest of Greece catches a tiny bite at sunset.

Weather at home is just hot.

Clear dawn to dusk, near twenty-seven early, peaking around thirty-five in the afternoon, still clinging to the high twenties into the evening.

No rain at all.

The Meltemi blows from the north at roughly six metres a second — breezy, but it won't cool you.

Sunset's around twenty past eight, and with heat and wind like this, fire risk stays high near the hills.

— personal items —

Gaming, and this one's on the clock: Epic's giving away Beacon Pines, an eerie little storybook mystery, and We Were Here Together, a two-player co-op puzzler — but only through tomorrow.

Claim them now even if you play later; once they're yours, they're yours.

Caravan SandWitch is up next.

And if you want something new to sink into, Marvel Tokon just dropped — a four-on-four tag-team fighter from the Guilty Gear crew.

And your learning bite.

Word of the day: smear — pressing the sole of your shoe flat against bare rock with no real foothold, trusting pure friction to hold your foot.

And a productivity trick: eat the frog — do your ugliest, most-dreaded task first thing, before the day fills up.

Everything after it feels lighter.

That's Tuesday — hot, quiet, and yours to shape.

Drink water, dodge the sun, and grab those games before they're gone.
